c1.prompt:
Create a single cohesive scientific diagram illustration for a top-tier CS conference paper.

## Content to Draw
Draw an overview diagram of the entire Early Experience paradigm, emphasizing the high-level flow from data to dual training methods.

Layout: Use a left-to-right flow across the page.

On the far left, place a teal (#2CA8A8) cylinder labeled "Expert Dataset D_expert" with a smaller subtitle "{(s_i, a_i)}" and in parentheses "expert state–action pairs" in smaller gray text. From this cylinder, draw a thick horizontal arrow to the right into a large light-gray (#F5F5F5) rounded rectangle spanning the central area, labeled at the top border "Early Experience: Data Construction & Dual-Method Training".

Inside this large rectangle, divide the space visually into two stacked rows: the top row labeled "Data Construction" (small title on the left, dark gray), and the bottom row labeled "Dual-Method Training".

In the top row, draw a mid-sized blue (#4A90D9) box labeled "Rollout Generation" with a subtitle "construct D_rollout". It should be connected with an arrow from the left border where the expert dataset arrow enters. From the right side of this "Rollout Generation" box, show a teal cylinder labeled "Rollout Dataset D_rollout" with subtitle "{(s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j)}".

In the bottom row, directly under the rollout cylinder, place two parallel branches: on the lower-left, a purple (#8E44AD) rounded rectangle titled "Implicit World Modeling (IWM)" and on the lower-right, an orange (#E67E22) rounded rectangle titled "Self-Reflection (SR)". Both should receive arrows from the expert dataset (top-left) and/or rollout dataset (top-center), indicating their inputs. At the far right, merge arrows from both IWM and SR into a dark blue (#1F4E79) box titled "Updated LLM Policy π".

Add a small caption under the whole central rectangle: "Core flow: Data Construction → Dual-Method Training (IWM + SR)" in light gray italics. Maintain a clean, NeurIPS-style, minimalistic look with thin arrows and sans-serif fonts.

## Image Specifications
- Aspect Ratio: 2:1 (width:height) - MUST be preserved
- Style: Professional scientific illustration, flat 2D vector style
- Colors: Professional muted tones (Morandi palette)
  - Use blues (#4A90D9, #5B9BD5) for main modules
  - Use teals (#66c2a5, #7ECFC0) for data/datasets
  - Use coral (#fc8d62) for highlights/accents
  - Use dark gray (#333333) for text
- Background: Solid white
- Font: Clean sans-serif style

## Visual Style Guidelines
- Clean geometric shapes with rounded corners
- Minimalist design, no unnecessary decorations
- Clear visual hierarchy
- Professional arrows and connectors
- Readable text labels (not too small)

## IMPORTANT - DO NOT Include
- Photorealistic elements or textures
- Heavy 3D effects or shadows
- Gradients on shapes (flat colors only)
- Busy or cluttered backgrounds
- Watermarks or signatures

Generate a single, cohesive image with all elements described above.

c2.prompt:
Create a single cohesive scientific diagram illustration for a top-tier CS conference paper.

## Content to Draw
Depict the detailed data construction pipeline: from expert data to rollouts with expert and non-expert actions.

Layout: A step-by-step pipeline flowing left to right.

On the far left, draw a teal (#2CA8A8) cylinder labeled "Expert Dataset D_expert" with the formula "{(s_i, a_i)}" inside. To the right, show an individual state–action pair: draw a small rounded square labeled "Expert state s_i" (light gray fill) above a small rounded square labeled "Expert action a_i" (light teal outline). Group them with a thin bracket or light box labeled "sample from D_expert".

From "Expert state s_i", draw a thick arrow to a blue (#4A90D9) rounded rectangle labeled "Initial LLM Policy π_0". From this policy box, fan out K thin arrows to the right into K small, horizontally aligned rectangles, each labeled "a_i^1", "a_i^2", ..., "a_i^K". Above this group, add the label "Sample K non-expert candidate actions {a_i^1, ..., a_i^K}" in small text. Color these candidate action boxes light yellow (#F9E79F) to distinguish from the expert action a_i (which can be light teal).

Next, show a stylized environment icon: a simple gray monitor or globe shape labeled "Environment" centered to the right. From the expert action a_i, draw an arrow down-right into the environment with label "execute a_i"; from each candidate action a_i^j, draw thin arrows into the same environment labeled "execute a_i^j".

On the right side of the environment, show resulting future states: one light-gray rounded square labeled "s_{i+1} (from a_i)" and a row of K light-gray rounded squares labeled "s_i^1, s_i^2, ..., s_i^K (from a_i^j)". Use thin arrows from the environment to each state box.

Finally, group the triplets into a teal cylinder on the far right labeled "Rollout Dataset D_rollout" with formula "{(s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j)}". Add a small annotation below: "future states as reward-free supervision" in gray italics.

## Content to Draw
Illustrate the Implicit World Modeling (IWM) branch where the LLM predicts future states from (s_i, a_i^j).

Layout: Left-to-right flow with emphasis on sequence prediction.

On the far left, draw a teal (#2CA8A8) cylinder labeled "Rollout Dataset D_rollout" with the formula "(s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j)". From it, draw an arrow to a light-gray grouping box labeled at the top "Training sample". Inside this box, depict the input as two stacked rounded rectangles on the left: the top one labeled "state s_i (tokens)" and the bottom one labeled "action a_i^j (tokens)", both with light outlines. To the right inside the same grouping, show a rounded rectangle labeled "target future state s_i^j (tokens)".

From the input (s_i, a_i^j), draw a thick arrow to a central dark blue (#1F4E79) module representing the LLM policy. Make it a wide rounded rectangle with a subtle Transformer icon or stacked layers, labeled "LLM Policy π (world modeling head)". From the right side of the LLM box, draw a sequence of small token boxes (little squares) forming "predicted s_i^j". Below them, draw another aligned sequence labeled "true s_i^j". Connect corresponding tokens with faint gray vertical lines, and draw a red dashed bracket around both sequences.

Next to this comparison, draw a small red loss icon (e.g., a hexagon) labeled "NLL loss" with the formula "-log p_π(s_i^j | s_i, a_i^j)" under it in small math font. Use arrows from the predicted vs. true token sequences into the loss icon, and then a back arrow from the loss icon to the LLM box labeled "gradient update".

At the bottom of the chunk, add a small caption: "IWM: LLM internalizes environment dynamics by predicting future states" in gray. Use purple accent lines or a purple (#8E44AD) title bar at the top of the whole chunk saying "Implicit World Modeling (IWM)".

## Content to Draw
Depict the Self-Reflection (SR) branch where the model compares expert vs non-expert outcomes and generates explanations.

Layout: A comparison structure from left to right, then downward into reflection generation.

On the left, draw a teal (#2CA8A8) cylinder labeled "Expert Dataset D_expert" with "(s_i, a_i)" and next to it a teal cylinder labeled "Rollout Dataset D_rollout" with "(s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j)". From both, arrows converge into a light-gray comparison panel centered in the figure.

Inside this comparison panel, on the left, show a column labeled "Expert path" with two stacked boxes: a rounded rectangle labeled "state s_i" and below it "expert action a_i"; to the right of these, a box labeled "future state s_{i+1}". Use a teal border for this column. On the right of the panel, show a parallel column labeled "Non-expert path" with "state s_i" (shared input, maybe highlighted as the same object), below it "non-expert action a_i^j", and to the right "future state s_i^j". Use a light yellow border for this column.

Between the expert future state s_{i+1} and non-expert future state s_i^j, draw a double-headed arrow labeled "compare outcomes". Above or below the panel, add a small orange (#E67E22) circular icon with a thought bubble symbol, connected to the comparison with a thin arrow.

To the right of the comparison panel, draw an orange rounded rectangle representing the LLM in reflection mode, labeled "LLM Policy π (reflection mode)". From the comparison panel, draw an arrow into this box with the label "input: (s_i, a_i, a_i^j, s_{i+1}, s_i^j)" in small text.

From the right side of this reflection LLM box, draw a text bubble or document icon in light orange labeled "natural language explanation c_i^j" and, in smaller text below, "why expert action is better".

Finally, show a teal cylinder at the far right labeled "Reflection Dataset D_refl" with the formula "{(s_i, a_i^j, c_i^j)}". An arrow from the explanation bubble should feed into this cylinder. At the top of the chunk, add a title bar in orange: "Self-Reflection (SR): Generate comparative explanations".

c5.prompt:
Create a single cohesive scientific diagram illustration for a top-tier CS conference paper.

## Content to Draw
Show the joint training of the LLM policy on expert actions and reflection explanations, integrating signals from D_expert and D_refl.

Layout: Two input datasets at the left converging into a central LLM, with dual outputs and losses.

On the left, place two vertically stacked cylinders. The upper cylinder is teal (#2CA8A8) labeled "Expert Dataset D_expert" with "(s_i, a_i)". The lower cylinder is teal with an orange rim labeled "Reflection Dataset D_refl" with "(s_i, a_i^j, c_i^j)". From each cylinder, draw arrows to a central batching box: a light-gray rounded rectangle labeled "Mixed Training Batches" with a subtitle "expert + reflection samples".

From this batching box, draw a thick arrow to a large dark blue (#1F4E79) rounded rectangle representing the shared LLM policy. Label it "LLM Policy π (shared parameters)" with a smaller subtitle "joint IL + SR training". Inside the LLM box, visually split the right half into two vertically stacked output heads with faint dividing line: the upper head labeled "Action head" and the lower head labeled "Reflection head".

From the "Action head", draw an arrow to the right into a set of small boxes labeled "predicted action distribution" with the target "expert action a_i" shown below in a light teal box. Next to them, place a blue loss icon labeled "Action loss (e.g., NLL)" with formula "-log p_π(a_i | s_i, context)".

From the "Reflection head", draw an arrow down-right into a sequence of token boxes labeled "predicted explanation c_i^j"; under that, show "true explanation c_i^j" as another sequence. Connect to an orange loss icon labeled "Explanation loss" with formula "-log p_π(c_i^j | s_i, a_i^j)".

Merge arrows from both loss icons back into the LLM box with a bracket labeled "joint optimization". At the far right, place a bold dark blue box labeled "Trained Early Experience Policy π*". An arrow from the central LLM plus losses should point to this final box, indicating the outcome of training.

Add a small caption at the bottom: "Policy learns to output both optimal actions and explanatory reflections" in gray italics.
